reading: The output is a fixed 3x3 pattern of 8 chosen by the input's most common non-background colour: 1 -> [008,880,080], 3 -> [088,080,080], 2 -> [000,888,000].

slots.class: most frequent non-background colour of the input

why: the output depends only on the majority colour; equal majority colours give identical outputs
invariants: output is always 3x3 with colours 0 and 8

reading: Each isolated single cell gets a 3x3 ring around it whose colour depends on the cell colour: 3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1; the centre cell stays.

slots.shape: the 8 neighbours of each marker (3x3 ring)
slots.colour: train key on the marker colour: 3->6, 8->4, 2->1

why: every marker's 8 neighbours become key(marker colour); nothing else changes

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into a grid of (number of background cells) x (number of background cells) blocks; the first k blocks in reading order (k = number of foreground cells) hold a copy of the input, the rest are empty.
why: each output block is the input or empty; copies = fg pixel count, filled row-major; blocks per side = bg pixel count
invariants: block contents are exact copies of the input

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled up by 3: every cell becomes a 3x3 block of its colour.
why: output cell (y,x) equals input cell (y//3, x//3)

reading: Four isolated 5-cells mark the sides of a box; a rectangle outline in the colour of the central shape is drawn one cell inside the markers (rows/cols just inside the topmost, bottommost, leftmost and rightmost markers).

slots.bounds: markers: top marker row+1, bottom marker row-1, left marker col+1, right marker col-1

why: the outline passes exactly one cell inside each of the four markers; everything else unchanged
invariants: markers and the central shape unchanged

reading: Full separator lines cut the grid into equal cells; one cell holds a pattern, which is copied into every cell whose row index and column index have the same parity as that cell's (every second cell in both directions).

slots.cells: blocks cut by separator rows and columns
slots.unit: contents of the one non-empty cell
slots.anchors: cells with (row index, col index) congruent mod 2 to the source cell

why: every same-parity cell equals the source cell; other cells and separators unchanged
invariants: cells of the other parity stay empty

reading: The top row (above a full 5 separator) lists colours c0,c1,c2,...; around the single marker below, concentric square rings are drawn: ring k (Chebyshev distance k) gets colour ck, clipped at the grid edge.

slots.centre: the single marker cell below the separator
slots.palette: header row cells left to right up to the last non-zero
slots.ring colour: palette[k] for cells at Chebyshev distance k from the centre

why: every cell within distance len(palette)-1 of the marker has palette[distance]; area outside unchanged
invariants: header and separator rows unchanged (pair 0 also shows the last header colour 8 replaced by 5)

reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the grid; at each diagonal corner of it a 2x2 block (clipped by the grid) is painted in the colour of the diagonally opposite cell of the block.

slots.subject: the 2x2 four-colour block
slots.targets: the four 2x2 areas diagonally adjacent to the block's corners
slots.colour: top-left area gets bottom-right colour, top-right gets bottom-left, bottom-left gets top-right, bottom-right gets top-left

why: each corner area is uniformly the opposite block colour; block unchanged

reading: Four L-shaped corner brackets mark a rectangle; the 1-pattern inside each rectangle is completed by mirroring it about the rectangle's centre line (left-right or up-down, whichever makes it symmetric), and stray 1-cells outside every rectangle are erased.

slots.frames: rectangles bounded by four corner brackets of one colour
slots.subject: 1-cells inside each frame
slots.axis: the frame's vertical or horizontal centre line

why: inside each frame the 1-pattern is symmetric about the frame's centre line; no 1 lies outside a frame

reading: Full 5 lines cut the grid into blocks; the top-left block is filled with 1, the centre block (middle row band and middle column band) with 2, and the bottom-right block with 3.

slots.cells: blocks cut by full separator rows and columns
slots.targets: first block (top-left), middle block, last block (bottom-right)

why: exactly those three blocks are filled; separators and other blocks unchanged
